properties.statement: THE WHOLE ORIENTATION SURFACE AFTER FOUR MERGES (#303–#306), measured from merged main on reflow2's own design. Bytes on the wire: open_questions 871 · what_next 3,157 · vocabulary_coverage 3,438 · graph_report_markdown 6,172 · loop_status 13,637 · graph_report 15,485 · detect_gaps 26,096 · detect_defects 26,169. BEFORE: graph_report ~334,000 · detect_gaps 157,785 · loop_status ~146,000 · detect_defects ~93,000 (the 'before' figures are the payload doubled, because every reply was sent twice). EVERY READ A SESSION MAKES TO ORIENT NOW FITS. || ⭐ THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THE NUMBERS: FOUR TOOLS NEEDED THREE DIFFERENT MECHANISMS, AND REACHING FOR A BUDGET EVERY TIME WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG THREE TIMES OUT OF FOUR. (1) `detect_gaps` — a genuine budget: measure the payload, drop the cheapest information first, say what was withheld and how to get it. (2) `graph_report` — nothing to budget; 91.5% was one list nobody asked for, withheld behind a flag with a digest that already existed. (3) EVERY reply — not big, DOUBLED: the payload went out as both `structuredContent` and a text block, and removing that alone fixed `loop_status` outright (72,886 and refused → 13,637) and CANCELLED A PLANNED PIECE OF WORK. (4) `detect_defects` — not big, REPETITIVE: 52% was three paragraphs repeated across 50 rows, so nothing needed withholding at all. ⇒ ASK WHETHER A REPLY IS BIG, DOUBLED, OR MERELY REPETITIVE BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING. Each answer has a different fix and only one of them is a budget. || ⭐ AND MEASURE BEFORE YOU CUT, EVERY TIME. On `detect_gaps` the guess would have been the id lists — they were 35%, capping them was not enough, and only the prose got it under a cap. On `graph_report` the clue was already on the wire: the MARKDOWN rendering of the same report was 27× smaller than the JSON one. On `loop_status` measuring first meant not building at all. || WHAT IS STILL OPEN: 113 of 197 Verification names carry whole reports (longest 654 words) — the replies no longer flood, but the reports are still in the wrong field, and that is a DATA problem in this design rather than a code one. The `graph_report` digest is flat in the PASSING remainder only, so a design mid-build with two hundred `planned` checks would be large again — real, unmeasured, deliberately not built for. || SOURCE: measured 2026-08-23 from merged main (0014ca6), driving the built binary over real stdio, one process, one sweep.
